mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is causally linked to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, with no threshold conditions required for the signal to be active. This reflects the monetary policy transmission channel where accommodative rates reduce discount rates for equity valuation.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for FEDFUNDS against 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in a 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals a deteriorating labor market, which typically precedes reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE against 5-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising monetary policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%) and a tightening labor market (UNRATE < 3.5%) signals an overheating economy that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle with strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% AND UNRATE < 3.5%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (FEDFUNDS * UNRATE) against 60-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, high housing starts (HOUST > 1300) signal overbuilding and potential economic overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1300 during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC for HOUST against 20-day SPX returns in late-cycle expansion is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of total employment (PAYEMS) reflects a robust labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, regardless of the absolute level.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for PAYEMS against 5-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between PAYEMS and 5-day SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in a 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) below 500,000 million dollars indicates weakening consumer demand, which typically reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS < 500000, or the Rank IC for RSAFS against 60-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO > 107) combined with falling housing starts (HOUST < 1280) signals a supply-demand mismatch where strong manufacturing output is not matched by housing demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO > 107 AND HOUST < 1280, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (INDPRO * HOUST) against 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 1.5%), high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 250) signals aggressive policy responses that compress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle with high inflation
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 250, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL against 5-day SPX returns in monetary tightening regimes is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
